section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
section.description: Answers to the most common questions about this page.

items.q: What does this page do?
items.a: It lists the Discord servers tied to your account so you can pick one to manage, or invite the bot to a server where it isn't yet present.

items.q: Why is one of my servers missing from the list?
items.a: Only servers where you are the owner or have the Manage Server permission appear here. Make sure you have that role on the server in Discord and refresh the page.

items.q: What happens when I click ‘Add Bot’?
items.a: Discord's invite dialog opens. After granting the recommended permissions, the bot joins the server and the entry switches to 'Added' here.

items.q: I added the bot but it still shows as not added — why?
items.a: Discord caching can delay the change. Wait a few seconds and refresh; if it persists, kick and re-invite the bot.

items.q: How can I search through my servers?
items.a: Use the search box at the top — the list filters in real time as you type.

items.q: How is the list ordered?
items.a: Servers that already have the bot come first, followed by other servers where you can manage the bot. Within each group the order is alphabetical.

items.q: Do I have to configure each server separately?
items.a: Yes — settings are per-server. Pick a server and configure its modules from the dashboard one by one.

items.q: Which permissions should I grant when inviting the bot?
items.a: Keep the default invite permissions. Cutting them down may break features (role assignment, message deletion, voice channel creation, etc.).

items.q: A newly added server isn't showing up?
items.a: You don't need to log out — just hit the refresh button at the top right. If it still doesn't appear, sign out of the panel and back in once.

items.q: How do I switch back after picking a server?
items.a: Click the server name in the sidebar and choose ‘Switch Server’, or go directly to /apps.

items.q: Why am I being shown this page?
items.a: You're redirected here when no server is selected, or the server you tried to open is not accessible to your account.

items.q: Are all my servers shown here?
items.a: No — only the ones you can manage (owner or Manage Server permission) appear in this list.

items.q: What should I do if the list is empty?
items.a: Make sure you have the Manage Server permission on at least one Discord server. If you've just been promoted, refresh the page.

items.q: What happens after I select a server?
items.a: It becomes your active server and you're redirected to the dashboard. All sidebar settings now apply to that server.

items.q: I picked the wrong server — how do I switch?
items.a: Click the server name at the top-left and use ‘Switch Server’, or pick another from /apps.

items.q: What is the icon next to each server?
items.a: It's the Discord server icon. If a server has none, the first letter of the name is shown instead.

items.q: The list isn't refreshing after a Discord change?
items.a: Sign out of the panel and sign back in. That refreshes the Discord session and updates the list.

items.q: Can I manage a server I don't own?
items.a: Yes, but only if you have the Manage Server permission. Otherwise Discord doesn't expose it as manageable.

items.q: What if the chosen server doesn't have the bot yet?
items.a: You're sent to the bot invite flow first; once the bot is in, your selection continues.

items.q: Can I open a server directly via URL?
items.a: Yes — visit /dashboard/<serverId>. If you lack permission you'll be redirected back here.

items.q: Why am I seeing this page?
items.a: An unexpected error happened during your action. It can be caused by a temporary outage, an expired session, or a permission issue.

items.q: How can I get past the error?
items.a: Refresh the page first. If the issue stays, sign out and back in; if it persists, contact support.

items.q: What do these error codes mean?
items.a: 401: session expired, 403: you don't have permission, 404: resource not found, 500: server error, 503: service temporarily unavailable.

items.q: Will my data be lost?
items.a: No. Saved settings are kept in the database — this error only affected the failed request.

items.q: Is the ‘Try again’ button safe to use?
items.a: Yes. It only retries the last request and won't create duplicate records.

items.q: I keep getting the same error — what now?
items.a: Clear your browser cache, then re-select the server from /apps. Network outages may also be the cause.

items.q: The bot works fine but the panel errors out?
items.a: The bot's link to Discord is independent. The panel API can have temporary hiccups — try again in a few minutes.

items.q: Should I report this error?
items.a: Sharing the error code and what you were doing speeds up fixes. Open a ticket from the Help Center.

items.q: Does this happen on mobile only?
items.a: Some browsers aggressively clear session cookies. Update your browser or try from a desktop.

items.q: Is there a backup of my data?
items.a: Panel settings are stored per guild. Use Audit Logs to review change history for important updates.

items.q: What does this dashboard show?
items.a: A live overview of the selected server — summary metrics (members, activity, tickets), quick-access module cards, and links to analytics and ticket inbox.

items.q: Why is the member count different from Discord?
items.a: It reflects what the bot has cached. Discord propagates events with a slight delay so a few minutes of lag can occur.

items.q: Which modules can I open from here?
items.a: Quick-access cards lead to Welcome, Moderation, Log Channel and a few other commonly used pages.

items.q: What does the recent activity panel list?
items.a: A summary of the most recent significant actions performed by the bot (welcome, log delivery, moderation).

items.q: What does ‘Active’ on a module mean?
items.a: The module's switch is on and the required channel/role configuration is valid.

items.q: The bot looks offline — what should I do?
items.a: Check the bot's role and your network in Discord. If the issue persists, raise a support ticket from the Help Center.

items.q: Is this data live or cached?
items.a: It's fetched on page load and refreshed every 30 seconds. Use the page refresh for an immediate update.

items.q: Who can see this page?
items.a: Anyone with Manage Server permission. There is no separate authorisation for moderators.

items.q: Where can I see deeper analytics?
items.a: The Statistics Channel, Invite Leaderboard and Reports pages provide deeper metrics.

items.q: What is this page for?
items.a: It greets you on first sign-in and briefly explains how the panel is laid out.

items.q: Will it show every time I open the panel?
items.a: No — only on your first visit or right after the bot is invited. Later visits open the dashboard directly.

items.q: Where should I go from here?
items.a: We recommend starting with General Settings and Log Channel, then enabling specific modules (welcome, moderation, etc.).

items.q: Do I need to configure everything right now?
items.a: No — modules can be enabled and configured at any time. Modules without configuration simply stay inactive.

items.q: Are there walkthroughs or videos?
items.a: Yes. The Help Center page has short module-by-module guides.

items.q: Can I skip the onboarding?
items.a: Use the Skip button to jump straight to the dashboard.

items.q: Multiple admins manage our server — do they all see the same view?
items.a: Yes. Anyone with Manage Server gets the same panel; their changes are tracked in audit logs.

items.q: Which modules are usually configured first?
items.a: Welcome message, Moderation, Log Channel, Autorole and Birthdays are the most common starting points.

items.q: Is there a paid plan or subscription?
items.a: No. There is no paid tier in the panel; core modules are free. Per-server usage limits are shown in the dashboard.

items.q: Can I disable a module I don't need?
items.a: Yes. Each module has a switch — your data is preserved and the module can be re-enabled later.

items.q: What is this page for?
items.a: An in-panel task tracker for your server's management work. You can create tasks, change their status and assign them.

items.q: How do I create a task?
items.a: Click ‘New task’, enter a title and optional description, then choose the assignee and tags.

items.q: Who can see these tasks?
items.a: Anyone with Manage Server permission on this server. Tasks are server-scoped and don't bleed into other servers.

items.q: What happens to completed tasks?
items.a: They stay under the ‘Completed’ tab. They are not deleted unless you remove them manually.

items.q: Can I import or export tasks?
items.a: Yes — ‘Import’ accepts JSON/CSV for bulk creation, and ‘Export’ downloads the current list.

items.q: Do task changes show up in Discord?
items.a: Yes — if a log channel is configured, creation and status changes are summarised there.

items.q: Can my team collaborate?
items.a: Yes. Each task supports comments and status updates; the audit log shows who changed what and when.

items.q: Are deleted tasks recoverable?
items.a: No — deletion is permanent. Use the ‘Completed’ status if you want a soft archive instead.

items.q: How do assignees get notified?
items.a: Users with DMs open are notified through Discord; otherwise the task only shows up in the panel.

items.q: Can tasks be managed via Discord commands?
items.a: Not yet — they are panel-only for now. Slash command integration is on the roadmap.

items.q: What does the Help Center contain?
items.a: Module-by-module usage guides, common issues, and an option to open a support ticket.

items.q: I can't find my topic — what now?
items.a: Try the search box with relevant keywords. If nothing matches, open a ticket from the Support form.

items.q: How do I contact support?
items.a: Use the ‘Contact us’ button at the bottom or join our Discord support server.

items.q: How fast does support respond?
items.a: Typically within 24 hours during business hours. Busy servers get prioritised.

items.q: How should I file a bug report?
items.a: Include the page where it happened, reproduction steps and any error code/screenshots. Reproducible scenarios get fixed faster.

items.q: Is there a community forum?
items.a: Yes — our Discord support server has community channels where you can ask others.

items.q: How do I send sensitive information?
items.a: Use the support form for private channels. Avoid posting tokens or personal info in public channels.

items.q: Is there developer documentation?
items.a: Yes — the ‘Documentation’ link gives detailed module guides.

items.q: Is there an AI assistant?
items.a: An in-panel assistant is currently in beta. When available it appears in the search box.

items.q: Where do I send feature suggestions?
items.a: Choose the ‘Suggestion’ category in the support form.

items.q: What does this module do?
items.a: It sends an automatic message when a new member joins. You can use a plain message, an embed, or a custom welcome card.

items.q: How do I include the user's name?
items.a: Use the placeholders {user}, {username} and {server}. They are replaced automatically when the member joins.

items.q: Can I send to both a channel and DM?
items.a: Yes — the channel message and the DM tab are independent and can be configured separately.

items.q: Why might a DM fail to send?
items.a: Members with DMs disabled or who blocked the bot can't be reached. The log channel records this as ‘Delivery failed’.

items.q: What does the welcome card look like?
items.a: A custom image with avatar + background + username. Colours and texts can be tuned from this page.

items.q: What's the difference between embed and plain text?
items.a: Embeds appear in a coloured card with title/description/footer; plain text is a regular Discord message.

items.q: Welcome message isn't being sent — what should I check?
items.a: 1) Module enabled, 2) target channel set, 3) bot has Send Messages, 4) the join was a real guildMemberAdd event (intents enabled in Discord Developer Portal).

items.q: Can I auto-assign a role?
items.a: Yes — the ‘Role to assign’ field gives the role to incoming members automatically.

items.q: Can I limit greetings to certain members?
items.a: Not directly here. For conditions use Autorole or a Custom Command.

items.q: Is there a preview?
items.a: Yes — the Preview button DMs you a simulation of the message without involving real members.

items.q: When is the goodbye message sent?
items.a: When a member leaves the server — voluntarily, by kick, or by ban.

items.q: Are banned users greeted with goodbye too?
items.a: By default yes. You can enable ‘Skip banned members’ to exclude them.

items.q: Which placeholders are supported?
items.a: {user}, {username}, {server}, {memberCount}.

items.q: I'd rather not announce departures?
items.a: Just disable the module — all goodbye messages stop.

items.q: Can I have separate templates for kick/ban/leave?
items.a: Yes — use the tabs to define a different template per reason.

items.q: Should the message go to the log channel instead?
items.a: Set ‘Target channel’ to the log channel, although a dedicated channel keeps things tidy.

items.q: Can the bot show the leaving user's avatar?
items.a: Yes — the DM card and embed thumbnail can include it.

items.q: Will the message be removed if the user rejoins?
items.a: No — past messages stay in the channel; the bot doesn't auto-delete them.

items.q: Can I use multiple languages per message?
items.a: The bot uses the server's language. Multi-language messages are not built-in.

items.q: Can the goodbye go to multiple channels?
items.a: Only one channel for now. For multiple channels you can use a Custom Command.

items.q: What is an embed?
items.a: A Discord message rendered inside a coloured card with title, description and additional fields.

items.q: What can I do on this page?
items.a: Pick a template, fill in title/description/footer/thumbnail/image and send the embed to a target channel.

items.q: How do I pick a colour?
items.a: Enter a hex value (e.g. #5865F2) or use the colour picker. The embed's left sidebar uses this colour.

items.q: Can I edit a sent embed?
items.a: Yes — provide the message ID and the existing embed is updated rather than reposted.

items.q: Can I add multiple fields?
items.a: Up to Discord's limit of 25 fields. Beyond that the page warns you.

items.q: Are placeholders supported?
items.a: Yes — {server}, {memberCount} and the variables you defined in custom commands are resolved at send time.

items.q: Can I schedule the embed?
items.a: This page is for instant sending. Use Scheduled Announcement for a delayed/recurring send.

items.q: How do I preview the final result?
items.a: The right side shows a live preview while you edit.

items.q: I sent a wrong embed — what now?
items.a: Find the message ID and use ‘Edit’, or delete it from Discord directly.

items.q: What if the bot lacks the embed permission?
items.a: Without ‘Embed Links’ Discord renders plain text. Add the permission to the bot's role.

items.q: What is a reaction role?
items.a: A system that gives or removes a role when a member reacts to a specific message with a specific emoji.

items.q: How do I pick the message?
items.a: Provide the channel and message ID, or have the bot create a fresh message for you.

items.q: How many emojis can a single message have?
items.a: Up to Discord's limit of 20 distinct reactions.

items.q: Can I use custom emojis?
items.a: Yes, custom server emojis work — the bot must be in the server hosting that emoji.

items.q: Does removing the reaction remove the role?
items.a: Yes by default. Enable ‘Sticky mode’ to keep the role even after removal.

items.q: Does it still work if the channel changes?
items.a: Yes — moving the message between channels is fine. Deleting the message disables it.

items.q: The bot says it can't assign the role?
items.a: Its top role must be above the role being assigned, and it needs Manage Roles.

items.q: Can I limit a member to a single role from a message?
items.a: Yes — turn on ‘Single choice’ to enforce one role per message.

items.q: How do I bulk delete old reaction roles?
items.a: Select the entry from the list and click Delete. Only the binding is removed; the message stays in the channel.

items.q: Are reaction role events logged?
items.a: Yes — if a log channel is configured, role grants/removals are recorded with member and message info.

items.q: What is a scheduled announcement?
items.a: A message sent automatically at a given date/time, optionally on a recurring schedule. It can be plain text or an embed.

items.q: Which time zone is used?
items.a: The server's configured time zone, or you can enter UTC explicitly.

items.q: How do I set up a recurring announcement?
items.a: Choose daily/weekly/monthly cadence, or use the Advanced field for cron-like patterns.

items.q: Can I cancel an announcement?
items.a: Disable or delete it from the list. Disabling preserves history while stopping deliveries.

items.q: Can I edit a scheduled message?
items.a: Yes, before send. Delivered copies aren't edited — use the Edit Message page if needed.

items.q: Does @everyone work?
items.a: Yes, if the bot has Mention Everyone. Otherwise the text shows but no notification fires.

items.q: Can I send the same message to multiple channels at once?
items.a: Each announcement targets a single channel. Duplicate it for additional channels.

items.q: Can I see past deliveries?
items.a: Yes — the History tab lists recent deliveries and their success/failure status.

items.q: What happens if a delivery fails?
items.a: Permission errors or deleted channels log a failure but don't stop the schedule. The next occurrence is retried.

items.q: Can I attach images?
items.a: Use embed mode — thumbnails/images are supported. Plain text doesn't allow image attachments here.

items.q: What does this module do?
items.a: It watches a YouTube/Twitch/RSS source and posts an announcement to the chosen channel whenever a new item appears.

items.q: Why don't I have to enter the full URL for YouTube/Twitch?
items.a: The bot prepends https://www.youtube.com/ or https://www.twitch.tv/ for you, so you only enter the channel name. This avoids broken URLs.

items.q: What format should an RSS link have?
items.a: A valid RSS/Atom URL (e.g. https://site.com/feed.xml). Use Preview to confirm the bot can fetch it.

items.q: How often is the source checked?
items.a: Default is every 15 minutes. Very short intervals may be rate-limited by the provider.

items.q: I'm not getting new content — what should I check?
items.a: Use Preview to verify the source is reachable. Make sure the channel name is correct and content was published recently.

items.q: Can I mention a role on each post?
items.a: Yes — pick a role under ‘Mention role’ and the bot pings it on delivery.

items.q: Will it post old content too?
items.a: No — only items published after the subscription is created are announced.

items.q: Can I edit the source URL later?
items.a: Yes — editing the URL clears the historical filter so it re-discovers from that point.

items.q: Will it catch YouTube live streams?
items.a: Yes — live streams trigger a separate announcement.

items.q: How do I create a poll?
items.a: Enter the question, options, target channel and duration, then click Create. The bot posts a message where reactions count as votes.

items.q: How many options can I add?
items.a: Up to Discord's limit of 20. Fewer options usually give clearer results.

items.q: What does multiple voting do?
items.a: When on, a member can react to multiple options. When off, only one vote is counted per member.

items.q: What happens when a poll ends?
items.a: The bot locks the message and posts a summary including the winning option. You can also end manually.

items.q: Can I see who voted?
items.a: Moderators can see the voter list in the ‘Vote details’ tab unless anonymous mode is enabled.

items.q: Can I edit a poll mid-flight?
items.a: Only the question and duration. Adding/removing options would invalidate existing votes.

items.q: Can I restrict voting to certain roles?
items.a: Yes — add roles to ‘Allowed roles’. Reactions from others won't count.

items.q: Are past polls archived?
items.a: Yes — they're listed on this page along with their results.

items.q: Can the result be applied automatically?
items.a: Today the bot only displays results. For automatic actions use a Custom Command.

items.q: Can I mention members in a poll?
items.a: Yes — @everyone or roles in the question or description, subject to bot permissions.

items.q: How do I start a giveaway?
items.a: Provide name, prize, winner count, channel and end date. The bot collects entries via reactions until the end date.

items.q: Which reaction enters the giveaway?
items.a: 🎉 by default. Anyone reacting with that emoji is added to the entry list.

items.q: Can there be multiple winners?
items.a: Yes — set Winner count. The bot draws that many random winners at the end.

items.q: Can I filter entrants?
items.a: Yes — restrict by role or minimum account age via Advanced settings.

items.q: Can I end a giveaway early?
items.a: Yes — pick it from the list and click End to finish immediately.

items.q: Can I redraw winners?
items.a: Yes — Reroll picks a new winner; original winners can be included or excluded.

items.q: Does the bot DM the winners?
items.a: If their DMs are open. Otherwise they are pinged in the channel.

items.q: What if the giveaway message is deleted?
items.a: It is auto-cancelled and logged. You'd need to start a new one.

items.q: Are giveaways archived?
items.a: Yes — the History tab keeps every giveaway and its winners.

items.q: Can I exclude specific members?
items.a: Yes, ‘Excluded roles’ and ‘Excluded users’ remove them from the draw.

items.q: How does the level system work?
items.a: Members earn XP by sending messages or spending time in voice. They level up at XP thresholds, and configured role rewards are granted automatically.

items.q: How much XP per message?
items.a: The ‘XP per message’ value. Random XP toggles randomness within a min/max range.

items.q: What does cooldown mean?
items.a: A wait time that prevents the same member from earning XP too fast. 30–60 seconds is recommended.

items.q: Can I exclude certain channels?
items.a: Yes — ‘Ignored channels’ skips spam or command channels.

items.q: How do I set role rewards?
items.a: Add level + role pairs in the Role Rewards table and enable the toggle.

items.q: Should the old reward role be replaced or stacked?
items.a: By default new roles stack. To keep just one, enable ‘Single role mode’.

items.q: Where do level-up notifications go?
items.a: To the configured notification channel or to DM. You can also disable notifications entirely.

items.q: Can I reset a member's XP?
items.a: Yes — individual or full server resets are available. The action cannot be undone.

items.q: Is XP transferable between servers?
items.a: No — XP is server-scoped and cannot be copied between servers.

items.q: Is there a leaderboard?
items.a: Yes — via Discord command (e.g. /level top) or the Statistics Channel module.

items.q: What does this page show?
items.a: It ranks members by how many invites they've brought into the server. Total, real (kept), left and fake invites are shown separately.

items.q: How are invites counted?
items.a: By tracking which invite link each new member used. The bot needs Manage Server permission.

items.q: What is a fake invite?
items.a: An invite from a very young account or a member who left immediately. They're flagged to filter spam.

items.q: Can I filter by date range?
items.a: Yes — use the date selector to view weekly/monthly/custom periods.

items.q: Can I configure invite rewards?
items.a: Yes — set role rewards based on invite count under ‘Invite rewards’. Manage Roles is required.

items.q: Can I see who a member invited?
items.a: Yes — clicking a row expands the list of invited users.

items.q: Numbers don't match Discord — why?
items.a: Discord caching can introduce a delay. Use ‘Sync’ to fetch the latest data.

items.q: Are pre-bot invites counted?
items.a: You can set a baseline value for older invites. Anything after the bot's join is real-time.

items.q: Can I reset the leaderboard?
items.a: Yes, ‘Reset’ wipes the whole server's tally. The action is permanent.

items.q: Can I display this leaderboard publicly?
items.a: Yes — surface it in voice channel titles via the Statistics Channel module.

items.q: What is an application form?
items.a: A multi-question form used for staff/jury/event applications. The bot collects answers and presents them to moderators for review.

items.q: How do I add fields to the form?
items.a: Use the panel-based form builder — add fields with label, type, and required flag. No JSON required.

items.q: Which field types are supported?
items.a: Short text, long text, number, date and select-list. Each field can be marked required or optional.

items.q: Where do members fill out the form?
items.a: The bot posts an ‘Apply’ button in the chosen channel. Members open it via DM or modal popup.

items.q: Where do answers go?
items.a: To the configured ‘Result channel’ as an embed, with Approve/Reject buttons for moderators.

items.q: Can approved applicants get a role?
items.a: Yes — set ‘Role on approval’ and the role is assigned automatically when approved.

items.q: Can the same member apply multiple times?
items.a: Subject to a cooldown (default 24h). New applications are allowed after that.

items.q: Are application histories kept?
items.a: Yes — the History tab lists every application and its status.

items.q: Will old answers change if I edit the form later?
items.a: No — old answers are pinned to the form version they were submitted on.

items.q: Can I have multiple forms (e.g. staff and event)?
items.a: Yes — define multiple forms with their own channels/roles/questions.

items.q: How is music played?
items.a: Run /play <track or URL> in the server. The bot joins your voice channel and starts playing. The panel only configures rules.

items.q: Which platforms are supported?
items.a: YouTube, Spotify (links), SoundCloud and direct audio URLs. Spotify playlists are matched and played track by track.

items.q: The bot won't join the voice channel?
items.a: It needs Connect and Speak permissions, and you must be in a voice channel when running /play.

items.q: How do I manage the queue?
items.a: /queue lists the queue, /skip skips, /pause pauses, /resume continues. The panel shows the currently playing track too.

items.q: What is the maximum queue length?
items.a: Queue limits are set per server and shown on the music priority page. Adjust via ‘Max queue’ where available.

items.q: Can I limit who can request songs?
items.a: Yes — ‘Allowed roles’ controls who can queue tracks.

items.q: How many songs can a user queue?
items.a: ‘Songs per user’ enforces an anti-spam limit.

items.q: Can I tune audio quality?
items.a: Use ‘Bitrate’: 96-128 kbps for low-bandwidth servers, 192-256 kbps where Discord allows.

items.q: What does the bot do after long silence?
items.a: It auto-disconnects after the idle timeout (configurable).

items.q: What is the ticket panel?
items.a: A button/menu that lets members open private support channels. Each click creates a dedicated ticket channel.

items.q: Who can see a ticket channel?
items.a: Only the requester, the configured ‘Ticket manager roles’ and selected moderators. It is hidden from everyone else.

items.q: Can I have multiple ticket categories (e.g. Bug/Question)?
items.a: Yes — enable multi-button/menu mode and define dedicated questions for each.

items.q: What happens when a ticket is closed?
items.a: The channel is archived or deleted; a transcript is sent to the log channel as HTML/embed.

items.q: What is a transcript?
items.a: A persisted record of all messages exchanged in the ticket, kept for later review.

items.q: Can a member open multiple tickets at once?
items.a: Off by default. Enable ‘Multiple tickets’ to allow several active tickets per member.

items.q: How are ticket channels named?
items.a: Auto-generated using a template like ‘ticket-{username}’ or ‘ticket-{count}’. The format is editable.

items.q: How do moderators join a ticket?
items.a: They are added automatically. ‘Claim’ assigns the ticket to a specific moderator.

items.q: Can I cap how many tickets exist?
items.a: Yes — per-server and per-user active limits are available.

items.q: How long is ticket data kept?
items.a: Active tickets are persistent; archives follow the retention setting (default 90 days).

items.q: What does this page cover?
items.a: Anti-spam, profanity filter, link/invite blocking, mention spam and message-flooding rules.

items.q: Can I disable a rule on certain channels?
items.a: Yes — ‘Ignored channels’ exempts them from moderation.

items.q: I want to spare specific roles from moderation?
items.a: Add them to ‘Ignored roles’; their messages bypass the rules.

items.q: What actions are available?
items.a: Delete, warn, time-out, kick, ban — based on configurable thresholds.

items.q: Can the bot delete my own messages?
items.a: Yes, unless your role is above the bot's role or you're in ‘Ignored roles’.

items.q: Are moderation events logged?
items.a: Yes — every action is forwarded to the configured log channel and visible under Moderation Logs.

items.q: How do I undo a wrong action?
items.a: Time-outs and bans have an Undo button. Deletions can't be reversed.

items.q: Can I customise the profanity list?
items.a: Yes — ‘Custom word list’ allows server-specific entries.

items.q: Does it catch obfuscation attempts?
items.a: Mostly yes via normalisation. For full coverage combine with AI moderation.

items.q: How does it integrate with AI moderation?
items.a: This page is keyword/pattern-based. For context-aware moderation, use the AI Moderation page in tandem.

items.q: How does AI moderation work?
items.a: The bot scores messages on toxicity, hate, sexual, harassment, self-harm and similar categories, then logs/deletes/timeouts based on thresholds.

items.q: What does sensitivity (Low/Normal/High) mean?
items.a: High triggers at lower scores and catches more messages. Low intervenes less. High is recommended on heavy-spam/troll servers.

items.q: Which channels should I exclude?
items.a: Channels where adult banter is allowed (e.g. 18+ general chat), bot test channels, and private chat channels.

items.q: Does it cover all languages?
items.a: It covers Turkish and the other 11 supported languages, including normalised text mixes.

items.q: Recommended action for personal attacks (insults)?
items.a: Log + warn first; time-out on repeat. Bans should be reserved for severe violations.

items.q: How can I reduce false positives?
items.a: Configure excluded channels, keep sensitivity at Normal, and add keyword exceptions if needed.

items.q: Can the bot show the actions it took?
items.a: Yes — ‘Review records’ lists recent triggers with channel/user/score.

items.q: How long is AI data retained?
items.a: 30 days by default. Disabling the module purges scheduled deletions.

items.q: Are there AI usage costs?
items.a: Standard usage is included in the server quota; exceeding limits shows an error in the panel.

items.q: Is every message scanned?
items.a: Use ‘Sample rate’ to scan a percentage (e.g. 50%, 100%). Useful for managing quota.

items.q: What does this page list?
items.a: Moderation-related records with filters applied; supported action types are only those shown in the UI — delete, warn, time-out, kick and ban are not all guaranteed.

items.q: How do filters work?
items.a: Action, rule type, channel, source (manual / AI / keyword filter) and date range can be selected. Multiple filters apply together.

items.q: Can I undo an action from here?
items.a: Undo is not offered for every action in this version; fix issues in Discord or the relevant module where possible.

items.q: Can I export the logs?
items.a: Yes — use the CSV or JSON buttons on the Records card to download the currently loaded (filtered) rows. The API query limit applies (up to 100 rows); split the date range and export again for longer periods.

items.q: What do the source values mean?
items.a: manual = manual action, ai = AI moderation, keyword = word/rule filter (labels may appear localized in the panel).

items.q: What if a member keeps getting hit?
items.a: Review their history — escalate the action (time-out → ban) for repeat offences.

items.q: How do I separate automated actions?
items.a: Narrow with the source filter by choosing AI moderation or keyword filter to see automated or rule-based cases.

items.q: What's in the detail view?
items.a: For the selected row: record id, message id, reason key, notice/error code, JSON reason parameters and optional AI score summary. User identifiers are stored as hashes.

items.q: How long are records kept?
items.a: 90 days by default. Records are auto-purged afterwards.

items.q: Bulk delete/cleanup?
items.a: This version has no bulk delete or archive button for filter results.

items.q: What is an audit record?
items.a: A timestamped log of any configuration change made through the panel or bot — who changed what and when.

items.q: Which changes are recorded?
items.a: Module toggles, channel/role selections, threshold updates, and form/template changes.

items.q: What is the before/after diff?
items.a: Side-by-side comparison of the previous and new state — easy to spot accidental changes.

items.q: What do action and resource filters mean?
items.a: Resource = which module the change touched (ai_moderation, ticket, etc.). Action = the operation (create/update/delete).

items.q: Can I revert a wrong change?
items.a: ‘Revert this change’ rolls back simple updates. Complex chains may need manual fixes.

items.q: Can records be edited?
items.a: No — audit logs are append-only. Only the system writes them.

items.q: How long are records retained?
items.a: 180 days by default.

items.q: Can I see who made each change?
items.a: Yes — the Actor field shows the Discord ID and name of the user.

items.q: Can I pull these logs via API?
items.a: Audit log entries can be viewed in the panel; export options vary by module.

items.q: Will many records hurt performance?
items.a: No — the page is paginated and filtered; data is fetched on demand.

items.q: What does this module do?
items.a: It maps server events (joins/leaves, message edits/deletes, voice changes, role changes, etc.) to log channels.

items.q: One channel for everything or per category?
items.a: You can route each log type to a separate channel, or use ‘New category + auto channels’ for a one-click setup.

items.q: Which log categories exist?
items.a: Member, message, channel, role, voice, invite, moderation, audit, and bot.

items.q: Why don't I see message logs?
items.a: The bot needs View Audit Log and Read Message History, and must be able to view the channel.

items.q: Logs are too noisy — how do I trim them?
items.a: Each log type has its own toggle; turn off the ones you don't need.

items.q: Embed or plain text?
items.a: Embeds by default, with colour and icon classification. Switchable to plain text for older clients.

items.q: Can I exclude channels from message logs?
items.a: Yes — ‘Ignored channels’ excludes sensitive/private channels.

items.q: What if the log channel is deleted?
items.a: The bot can't deliver and logs an error; you'll need to choose a new channel.

items.q: Is there log retention?
items.a: Discord keeps the messages per its policies. The panel additionally keeps a 90-day archive.

items.q: Can I restrict log channels by role?
items.a: Yes — make the channel moderator-only so members can't read it.

items.q: What is a custom command?
items.a: It lets you define a /command for your server. When members run it, the bot executes the configured action — typically sending a message.

items.q: What can the basic view do?
items.a: Plain message, embed reply and short info responses. For complex flows use the Advanced view.

items.q: How should the command name look?
items.a: Lowercase letters and dashes (-) only. Turkish characters are normalised (ş→s, ç→c).

items.q: Can I reuse a command name?
items.a: No — names are unique within the server. The form warns you if there's a collision.

items.q: Restrict who can run it?
items.a: Add roles to ‘Allowed roles’. Other roles get a permission error.

items.q: What is cooldown for?
items.a: A short wait per user to prevent spam — entered in seconds.

items.q: Restrict the command to a single channel?
items.a: Yes — enable ‘Limit to this channel’ and pick one.

items.q: What does ‘Pin command usages’ mean?
items.a: It locks the command's response — kept on the panel even if the server is wiped.

items.q: Are placeholders supported?
items.a: Yes — {user}, {server}, {channel} and others are filled in at runtime.

items.q: Does the command appear in Discord immediately?
items.a: Yes — but Discord caching may delay propagation by 5–10 minutes occasionally.

items.q: How is the advanced view different from basic?
items.a: Beyond messages, it supports role grants/removals, channel creation, member moves, embed sends, and chaining multiple actions per command.

items.q: Multiple actions per command?
items.a: Yes — add them to the Actions list and the bot executes them in order.

items.q: Does action order matter?
items.a: Yes. ‘Grant role then send message’ vs ‘send message then grant role’ produce different results.

items.q: Which role/member changes are possible?
items.a: Grant role, remove role, move member, kick from voice, apply timeout.

items.q: Are there conditional actions?
items.a: Yes — the Condition field can check role/channel state. If unmet, the command exits silently.

items.q: Can I accept arguments?
items.a: Yes — define slash parameters and reference them in your reply via {arg.name}.

items.q: What happens on error?
items.a: The bot stops at the first failed action and logs an entry to the audit log; later actions don't run.

items.q: Are there Quota-gated actions?
items.a: Webhook and API integration actions can be configured in the automation module; server quotas apply.

items.q: Can I dry-run a complex flow?
items.a: Yes — ‘Test it’ executes a dry-run on the live server.

items.q: Can I roll back to a previous version?
items.a: Yes — open the audit log entry and use ‘Revert to this version’ to make it active.

items.q: What is a temporary voice channel?
items.a: When a user joins the configured ‘lobby’ voice channel, the bot creates a private channel for them. It's removed when they leave.

items.q: Which channel should be the lobby?
items.a: Pick a regularly used voice channel (often ‘General Voice’) under ‘Lobby channel’.

items.q: Who controls permissions on the new channel?
items.a: The owner does — they can lock/unlock, set user limits, rename, kick members via commands/buttons.

items.q: Is the new channel created in the lobby's category?
items.a: By default yes. Pick a different category in ‘Under existing category’ to override.

items.q: What's the user limit?
items.a: Up to Discord's max of 99. Set the default with ‘User limit’.

items.q: Can I template the channel name?
items.a: Yes — ‘Temporary channel name’ supports {user} and {server}, e.g. ‘{user}'s Room’.

items.q: Does the bot delete the channel immediately?
items.a: Per ‘Channel deletion delay’ — instantly or after a few seconds when empty.

items.q: What if the owner leaves the server?
items.a: Ownership can be passed to the next eligible member or follow your policy. Otherwise the channel is removed.

items.q: What does ‘Sync with lobby permissions’ mean?
items.a: Role permissions on the lobby propagate to each new private channel — no manual setup needed.

items.q: How many temporary channels can exist concurrently?
items.a: Server quotas are shown in the panel; new records cannot be added when a limit is reached.

items.q: What is a statistics channel?
items.a: Voice channels whose names show server counters (members, online, bots, role count, invites).

items.q: Which counters are supported?
items.a: Total members, online, offline, bots, members in a role, total invites and custom counters.

items.q: How often does it update?
items.a: Every 5–10 minutes due to Discord rate limits. Faster updates aren't possible.

items.q: How is the channel name templated?
items.a: Use the ‘Template’ field where {value} is replaced by the counter, e.g. ‘Members: {value}’.

items.q: Who can speak in the channel?
items.a: Nobody by default — these channels are display-only, with @everyone Connect disabled.

items.q: Can I have multiple counters?
items.a: Yes — create as many statistics channels as you need, each with its own template.

items.q: The number looks wrong — what should I do?
items.a: Likely a Discord cache. Use ‘Sync’ to force a refresh.

items.q: Will the value still update if the bot is offline?
items.a: It freezes at the last value; updates resume when the bot is back online.

items.q: If I delete the channel, is the counter lost?
items.a: No — only the channel binding is removed. Re-link to a new channel any time.

items.q: What is autorole?
items.a: It assigns one or more roles automatically to new members, members matching certain criteria, or to bots.

items.q: Can I assign multiple roles?
items.a: Yes — pick several roles. All are assigned within Discord's role limits.

items.q: Can bots get auto-assigned a role?
items.a: Yes — the ‘Bot role’ field is separate and bots don't get the regular auto roles.

items.q: I'm getting a permissions error?
items.a: The bot's top role must be above the role being assigned, plus it needs Manage Roles.

items.q: Are there account-age conditions?
items.a: Yes — ‘Minimum account age (days)’ defers assignment until the threshold is met.

items.q: Does the age condition help against raids?
items.a: Yes — it filters out fresh/throwaway accounts during a raid.

items.q: Are existing members auto-assigned too?
items.a: Only new joiners by default. Use ‘Apply to all’ for a one-time bulk assignment.

items.q: Can I delay the assignment?
items.a: Yes — ‘Delay (seconds)’ lets you defer the role grant, useful as anti-raid.

items.q: What if a member removes the role themselves?
items.a: If ‘Re-apply’ is on, the bot reassigns it; otherwise it's a one-shot grant.

items.q: Can autorole events be logged?
items.a: Yes — the log channel records who got which role and when.

items.q: What does the birthday module do?
items.a: It congratulates members on the date they registered and optionally grants a temporary birthday role.

items.q: How do members register their birthday?
items.a: Via a bot command (e.g. /birthday) or a modal form. Only month/day is required; year is optional.

items.q: Is the year required?
items.a: No — month/day is enough. Including a year enables age calculation; without it only the celebration is sent.

items.q: What time of day is the celebration?
items.a: 09:00 server time by default. Configurable via ‘Check hour’.

items.q: Multiple birthdays on the same day?
items.a: The bot tags everyone in a single message — no spam.

items.q: How long does the birthday role last?
items.a: 24 hours by default (configurable in hours). It's removed automatically.

items.q: Can a member delete their data?
items.a: Yes — via their own command or a ‘Delete my data’ button shown to them.

items.q: Is age hiding possible?
items.a: Yes — members can register with month/day only, no age stored or shown.

items.q: What if there's no notification channel?
items.a: The module won't run. Configure both notification and (optional) public channels.

items.q: Are previous years celebrated again?
items.a: Yes — every year the same date triggers a celebration. If the user left, the data is kept but no notification is sent.

items.q: What does the reminder module do?
items.a: It sends a message at a date/time to a member or channel — events, deadlines, appointments.

items.q: One-shot or recurring?
items.a: Both. One-shot fires once; recurring uses daily/weekly/monthly schedules.

items.q: DM or channel?
items.a: Either — if DMs are closed and a channel is configured, that's used.

items.q: How are time zones handled?
items.a: The server time zone is the default. Members can use /timezone to set their own.

items.q: Multiple reminders per server?
items.a: Yes — each reminder runs independently. Server quota is shown in the panel.

items.q: If I delete a reminder, does the history get wiped?
items.a: No — past deliveries stay in their channels/logs. Only future occurrences are cancelled.

items.q: Can I tie reminders to events?
items.a: You can define a trigger that warns X minutes before start, integrated with Discord events.

items.q: Are placeholders supported in messages?
items.a: Yes — {user}, {date}, {time} are replaced at delivery.

items.q: Why didn't a reminder fire?
items.a: Possible bot permissions, missing channel, closed DMs, or the bot was offline. Check logs.

items.q: Is a reminder history kept?
items.a: Yes — the History tab shows the last 90 days of reminders.

items.q: What does the Reports page provide?
items.a: Visual analytics for growth, engagement, moderation events and invite performance, with charts and summaries.

items.q: Which time ranges are available?
items.a: Last 7/30/90 days and a custom date picker.

items.q: Can I download reports as PDF/Excel?
items.a: Yes — Export at the top right gives PDF or Excel.

items.q: How far back does data go?
items.a: 90 days retention by default. Use Excel exports for longer retention.

items.q: Are reports real-time?
items.a: No — they're recomputed daily. Use the Dashboard for near-real-time stats.

items.q: How is engagement measured?
items.a: Messages, voice time, invites, reactions and command usage. Bot messages are excluded.

items.q: Is there staff comparison?
items.a: Yes — ‘Staff performance’ shows mod actions, ticket response times, etc.

items.q: Can I filter by channel/role?
items.a: Yes — use the filters at the top right of each report.

items.q: Can I sort tables?
items.a: Yes — click a column header to toggle ascending/descending.

items.q: Why are some periods missing?
items.a: Bot downtime causes data gaps. Those windows are flagged in the ‘Missing intervals’ panel.

items.q: What does bot language mean?
items.a: It controls the language the bot uses for messages on this server. Choose among 12 supported languages.

items.q: Per-member language?
items.a: Server-wide for now. Per-user preferences are on the roadmap.

items.q: What's the fallback language?
items.a: Used when a translation is missing in the active language. Common picks are Turkish or English.

items.q: Will all messages refresh after I change language?
items.a: New messages use the new language. Past messages aren't edited (Discord doesn't allow it).

items.q: What happens with a missing key?
items.a: It falls back to the fallback language and a warning is raised.

items.q: Does language apply to custom commands?
items.a: No — custom command text is yours and is independent of bot language.

items.q: Can I add a new language?
items.a: Only the 12 supported languages are active. Suggest a new one via the support form.

items.q: Does AI moderation respect this language?
items.a: AI is multilingual and not affected by this setting. This page only controls bot messages.

items.q: Are language changes audited?
items.a: Yes — language changes appear in audit logs as configuration updates.

items.q: What does this page manage?
items.a: An overview of every server tied to your account — bot status and high-level configuration.

items.q: Can I remove the bot from a server?
items.a: Yes — Remove bot makes the bot leave. Your data is kept for 30 days and can be restored.

items.q: Can I rename a server here?
items.a: No — server names are managed in Discord. The panel reflects them.

items.q: Can I copy settings between servers?
items.a: Yes — ‘Copy configuration’ duplicates module setup to another server.

items.q: How do I diagnose a server-specific issue?
items.a: Pick the server and click ‘Run diagnostics’ — it checks permissions, channel/role references and subscription state.

items.q: Bulk operations across servers?
items.a: Yes — use the multi-select on the left to enable/disable modules in bulk.

items.q: When is bot data deleted?
items.a: 30 days after the bot leaves a server, the related data is auto-purged. Restore in time if needed.

items.q: Can I invite admins to the panel?
items.a: Anyone with Manage Server gets panel access automatically; there's no separate invite system.

items.q: What if a server is deleted in Discord?
items.a: After 7 days the panel record is archived per the data retention policy.

items.q: What is a custom bot?
items.a: Run a separate Discord bot under your own brand/avatar/commands while keeping the same core engine.

items.q: Where do I get a bot token?
items.a: From Discord Developer Portal > Application > Bot. Tokens are private — paste it carefully into the panel.

items.q: Where do I paste the token?
items.a: Into ‘Bot Token’. It is encrypted at rest and never shown again in plain text.

items.q: Multiple custom bots at the same time?
items.a: No — only one private bot can be registered per account.

items.q: Are commands the same as the main bot?
items.a: Core features are the same; name and avatar differ. You can rename commands.

items.q: My custom bot is offline?
items.a: Check the token, that the bot was added to Discord, and that the required intents are enabled. Errors are surfaced on this page.

items.q: How do I set the avatar?
items.a: Use the Bot Personalizer on the Custom Bot page to upload icon and banner, set the bot name, and configure status/activity text. When the bot is running, changes are applied to the Discord profile after save.

items.q: My token leaked — what now?
items.a: Reset the token in the Developer Portal and paste the new one. The old token instantly stops working.

items.q: Can multiple custom bots live in the same server?
items.a: You can only register one private bot per account. You may run it alongside the main Deveng bot on the same server.

items.q: Can I pause a custom bot?
items.a: Yes — ‘Pause’ stops the bot. Token and settings are kept for later.
